rv.q: Although billed as a developmental production, this fully staged musical is already well worth seeing at Theo Ubique Cabaret Theatre, where Grace Dolezal-Ng directs a charming, all-Asian American cast.
I recommend Baked! The Musical as part of your fall theater gazing.
“Baked! The Musical” at Theo Ubique has all the ingredients of a great show—energetic cast, delightful songs and more depth than your typical trope-filled love story.
Baked the Musical is a cute and likable show even if it does have some problems.
The fairest suggestion is that Baked! needs more time in the oven, more seasoning, and a pinch more of this and a dash less of that.
This is, however, a work of art in progress that’s still finding itself.
People going to Baked! should feel good about supporting a work in progress.
The show itself is a touching story about a family.

cn.t: This sweet, funny coming-of-age musical about an Asian-American teen selling edibles for Harvard tuition shows promise but needs more development, with critics praising its charm and cultural perspective while noting it's still a work in progress.
